items.question: Why doesn't the International Space Station fall down if gravity up there is still about 90% as strong as on the ground?
items.expected: It is falling: orbital velocity ~7.7 km/s means it falls around the Earth (free fall), hence weightlessness.

items.question: Why do historians argue about whether the Treaty of Versailles caused the Second World War?
items.expected: Keynes-style 'Carthaginian peace' view vs revisionists (Macmillan, Marks): terms were harsh but not crippling, reparations partly paid and cut (Dawes/Young, Lausanne 1932); enforcement failure, the Depression, appeasement and Hitler's choices matter more; 'stab-in-the-back' myth and war-guilt clause fed resentment.

items.question: In the Haber process, why do factories run at around 450 °C when Le Chatelier's principle says a lower temperature would give more ammonia?
items.expected: Forward reaction exothermic, so low T raises equilibrium yield, but the rate is too slow; ~400-450 °C with an iron catalyst and ~200 atm is a compromise between yield and rate; unreacted gas is recycled.

items.question: If one country is better at producing everything than another, why would it still gain from trading with it?
items.expected: Comparative advantage (Ricardo): opportunity costs differ; each specializes in the good with lower opportunity cost and total output rises; a worked example; caveats (distribution, adjustment costs, assumptions).
